name: The deflection
fires: Every single time the shield turns something away. Hundreds of times a run.
direction: Short, blunt, percussive. Bonk, doink, thok, bap, donk, pock. Mouth percussion is perfect — a finger popped out of your cheek, a tongue click, a flat closed-mouth thump. Keep every one under a third of a second and make them genuinely different from each other, because this is the sound you will hear more than any other.

name: Rock on rock
fires: Two pieces of debris knocking into each other, off to the side.
direction: Drier and smaller than the deflection — a knuckle on a table, a tut, a click. These are background, so they should never pull focus.

name: The balloon goes
fires: Death, in the level modes. The biggest moment in a run.
direction: A proper finger-in-cheek pop, a raspberry, and a sad lip-flap like a balloon deflating. Three, because dying to the same noise every time gets old fast.

name: The little noise after
fires: Immediately after the pop, under the game-over card.
direction: This is where the comedy is. A small defeated human sound — an "…ough", an "oh no", a long resigned sigh, a quiet "well." Underplay it. The flatter it is, the funnier.

name: The pickup
fires: Collecting a gem, and again on each step of a nerve chain.
direction: A short bright "boop", "nom", "yip", "hup". The game pitches these up as a chain builds, so keep them clean and stubby with no tail.

name: The near miss
fires: A block taken so late it scores the top multiplier.
direction: A sharp intake of breath. A tiny "hoo". The sound of somebody watching who thought that was going to go badly. Sharp and quick.

name: The fanfare
direction: Sing it with your mouth, deliberately naff — "ba-da-DAAA". A kazoo would be perfect. It should sound like a celebration that cost nothing.

name: The burst
direction: A whoosh. Blow past the mic, or a sharp "fwoom". Wind, not impact.

name: Something good happened
fires: A power-up, a second wind, a new phase of the mission.
direction: A rising three-note hum, an impressed "ooooh", a little "ta-daa". Warm.

name: The hatch opens
fires: When he appears at the side of the screen.
direction: A creak, a clunk, or a small throat-clear — the sound of somebody about to interrupt you. An "ahem" works beautifully here.

name: No
fires: Trying to buy something you cannot afford.
direction: A flat descending "nuh-uh", or a short buzzer with your mouth. Unimpressed.
